transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ll sit down to eat and end up putting away way more food than anyone else, more than I ever planned, and it really scares me. I just don't understand why this keeps happening to me at my age.
When you have these episodes of eating more food than planned, do you often feel a lack of control over your eating during those times?

Yes, it really feels like a switch flips off in my head and I just can't stop. Even when I'm telling myself to quit and feeling uncomfortably full, I just keep going. It's almost like I'm watching my own hands bring food to my mouth and I can't make them stop.
After these episodes of eating more than planned, do you ever try to compensate by purging, using laxatives, or excessively exercising to make up for the calories consumed?

It's hard to admit, but yes—sometimes I'll go into the bathroom, run the tap, and force myself to throw up or take extra laxatives to get the food out. Other times, I'll try to make up for it the next day by skipping meals entirely or walking laps around the block until my legs ache. This whole cycle of overeating and then trying to undo it happens about once or twice a week.
Can you tell me more about how often these episodes of binge eating followed by purging or compensating occur, and have you noticed any pattern or regularity to them over the past few months?

It's been a consistent pattern of at least once or twice every week for well over a year now, ever since my heart scare. It almost always happens with an evening meal, and then I spend the night or the next day trying to undo it by throwing up, skipping meals, or walking until it hurts.

Have you experienced any periods of time where you had three or more months without these episodes of binge eating followed by purging or compensating, or has this been a relatively continuous pattern over the past year?

No, there haven't been any breaks like that at all. It has been a continuous, ongoing pattern pretty much every single week since my heart scare about a year and five months ago. I haven't had any real relief or even a month's pause from it, let alone three.

Can you estimate how many times a month you engage in these binge eating episodes followed by purging or other compensatory behaviors, and have you noticed any significant weight fluctuations over the past year as a result?

It happens about four to eight times a month, pretty consistently over this past year. I haven't noticed any major weight swings, but I obsessively check the scale every morning and panic if it goes up by even a single pound. I'm just terrified that gaining any weight will trigger another heart attack and kill me.

Can you tell me if your binge eating episodes are always followed by purging, laxatives, or excessive exercise, or are there times when you binge eat without attempting to compensate for the calories?

Almost every single time I have one of those out-of-control episodes, I feel compelled to compensate in some way. The panic and guilt are so strong that I always try to 'make up for it'—whether that means forcing myself to throw up immediately afterward, or skipping meals and walking until my legs ache the next day. I just can't let myself eat like that without trying to undo it.
Are there times when you eat a large amount of food in a short period, feeling a lack of control, but without any subsequent purging, laxatives, or excessive exercise to compensate for the calories?

Honestly, it is very rare, if ever, that I don't try to compensate. The sheer panic and fear of gaining weight—and having another heart attack—is so overwhelming after an episode that I almost always feel forced to do something to make up for it. I just can't sit with that food in me, so I'll end up forcing myself to throw up, skipping my next meals, or walking until my legs ache.
